what: Official code for the Nature 2023 FunSearch paper: a frozen LLM evolves a `priority` function inside a problem skeleton while evaluators score candidates and islands of programs recycle the best as few-shot examples; ships the discovered cap-set, admissible-set, bin-packing and cyclic-graph artifacts.
architecture: Skeleton contract (implementation/funsearch.py): a specification must contain exactly one `@funsearch.run` function (the scorer, e.g. `evaluate(n) -> int`) and one `@funsearch.evolve` function to evolve (e.g. `priority(el, n)`); funsearch.main() seeds the initial body into all islands and launches Sampler/evaluator loops. cap_set/cap_set.ipynb shows the full skeleton — solve() builds a cap set greedily from the LLM-written priority, so the LLM evolves a scoring rule, not the object itself.

Prompt construction (implementation/programs_database.py): each of num_islands=10 Islands clusters programs by signature (the tuple of per-test scores); clusters are softmax-sampled with a temperature decaying linearly over 30,000 programs (init 0.1), shorter programs favored within a cluster, then `functions_per_prompt=2` implementations are score-sorted, renamed `_v0, _v1, ...` with docstrings 'Improved version of `_v{i-1}`', and the prompt ends with an empty `_v{n}` header for the LLM to continue.

Island resets as diversity pressure: every reset_period (14,400 s = 4 h) the weakest half of islands is wiped and re-founded from the best program of one random surviving island; results land back via register_program(program, island_id, scores_per_test), so generations stay attributable to the island that produced their prompt.

Evaluator gate (implementation/evaluator.py): _trim_function_body parses the continuation with ast, deleting trailing lines until it compiles, splices it into the template, and runs it in a Sandbox (abstract stub, 30 s timeout) on held test inputs — candidates calling an ancestor `_v*` version are rejected by _calls_ancestor, and only programs returning int/float scores on every input register. Both `LLM._draw_sample` and `Sandbox.run` raise NotImplementedError: no model, sandbox, or distributed infra ships (config defaults: num_samplers=15, num_evaluators=140, samples_per_prompt=4).
advantages: Ships the actual winning artifacts, not just the loop: the discovered priority functions that build a 512-cap in n=8 (previous best construction: 496) and a 1082-cap in n=9 (matching the previous best), admissible sets up to n=24, w=17, size 237,984, corner-free sets, cyclic-graph independent sets, and bin-packing heuristics with an OR3 (20 instances x 500 items) / Weibull 5k evaluation suite reporting excess over the L1 lower bound.

Program-space search yields inspectable mechanisms: the n=8 discovered priority's weight/reflection regularities were hand-distilled into build_512_cap(), an explicit construction of the 512-cap — the notebook walks from skeleton to discovered function to human-understandable structure.

The minimal reference LLM+evaluator loop (~640 lines across five files): every trick of the later, bigger systems — signature clustering, temperature schedules, island resets, few-shot score-sorted prompt ordering, ancestor-call rejection — is one short, copyable function.
run: No installation required — open the notebooks in Google Colab (cap_set/cap_set.ipynb, admissible_set, bin_packing, cyclic_graphs each have a Colab badge in the README). To run the pipeline yourself, implement the `LLM._draw_sample` and `Sandbox.run` stubs and call `funsearch.main(specification, inputs, config)` from implementation/funsearch.py (see implementation/specification_nonsymmetric_admissible_set.txt for a spec example).
note: Read programs_database.py's get_prompt/_generate_prompt first — score-sorted `_v0..._vn` few-shots ending in an empty header is the core trick. Then evaluator.py's _calls_ancestor anti-cheat. Run cap_set.ipynb's discovered priority to verify 512 (n=8) and 1082 (n=9) yourself.
_source_note: Read the README, all five implementation/*.py files (funsearch.py, sampler.py, programs_database.py, evaluator.py, config.py), the spec txt, and every cell of cap_set.ipynb and bin_packing.ipynb on main (Sep 2026). All numbers verified against source: 512/496 and 1082 caps, 237,984 admissible set, config defaults (10 islands, 2 fns/prompt, 4h reset, 0.1 temp / 30k period, 15 samplers, 140 evaluators, 4 samples/prompt, 30s timeout). Confidence high. Note: the README cites Nature (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06924-6 — the companion paper card is catalogued as nature-funsearch-2024 (print issue).
